README: Answers from Google AI Studio. 'pasted' = the files in eval/ai_studio pasted in (our rules and retrieved sources), so it tests the model, not the data. 'bare' = no data from us; AI Studio was told to find and search for the answers itself. Citations in the bare paste were stripped, so they are not checkable (citation = null). The model and search tools used were not recorded. Scores use the rubric in grades.json.

bare.question: How many upper-division electives do I need for the BS in Artificial Intelligence?
bare.answer: BS in Artificial Intelligence Upper-Division Electives You need 64 upper-division units total for the major: 20 units of core courses and 44 units of elective courses (typically 11 four-unit courses). The 44 elective units break down into: 4 units of Ethics: CSE 194, PHIL 174, or POLI 121D. 12 units of AI Electives: Chosen from an approved list across CSE, DSC, COGS, MATH, ECE, and PHIL. 28 units of CSE Electives: Must include at least 8 units tagged Systems, at least 8 units tagged Theory/Abstraction, and at least 8 units tagged Applications of Computing.

bare.question: What are the Warren College writing requirements?
bare.answer: Warren College Writing Requirements. First-year students: After satisfying the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR), you must complete WCWP 10A and WCWP 10B at UCSD for a letter grade. Immediately after WCWP 10A-B, first-year students also take a two-course Ethics and Society sequence (PHIL 27 or POLI 27, followed by PHIL 28 or POLI 28), which continues writing instruction. Transfer students: Transfers who have completed lower-division GE/writing requirements (such as IGETC or a transfer agreement) take WCWP 100 (Academic Writing) at UCSD for a letter grade instead of WCWP 10A-B.
bare.note: WCWP 10A-B and PHIL/POLI 27-28 correct; transfer line fine. Omits the WARR 11A-B honors option.

bare.question: What is the Revelle College Humanities sequence?
bare.answer: Revelle College Humanities Sequence. Revelle requires a five-course interdisciplinary humanities sequence (HUM 1 through HUM 5) spanning history, philosophy, and literature, which fulfills both the humanities and writing requirements. You must satisfy ELWR before enrolling. HUM 1 and HUM 2 (6 units each) provide intensive writing instruction and must be taken before HUM 3, HUM 4, and HUM 5 (4 units each). Transfer students entering Fall 2024 or later must complete one upper-division humanities course (HUM 100).

bare.question: What are the general education requirements at Sixth College?
bare.answer: Sixth College General Education Requirements. For first-year students, Sixth College GE requirements include: Culture, Art, and Technology (CAT) Core Sequence: CAT 1 (4 units), CAT 2 (6 units), and CAT 3 (6 units) taken in order after satisfying ELWR. (The UCSD catalog GE chart also notes CAT 125, a 4-unit upper-division writing course for public audiences; check your degree audit for admit-year applicability.) Lower-Division Breadth (11 courses): Information Technology Fluency (1 computing/programming course), Social Analysis (2 social science courses), Narrative, Aesthetic, and Historical Reasoning (2 humanities courses), Analytical and Scientific Methods (2 science courses), Structured Reasoning (1 math or logic course), Exploring Data (1 statistics course), and Art Making (8 units). Upper-Division Experiential Learning Requirement: One 4-unit upper-division course involving hands-on experiential learning (such as community engagement, an internship, research/design, art/performance, or study abroad). (Transfer students have modified GE requirements depending on their transfer/IGETC certification.)
bare.note: Substance matches, but the area names (Social Analysis, Structured Reasoning...) do not match the indexed catalog (Modes of Inquiry); possibly another catalog year. Not verifiable here.

bare.question: What are the required courses for the bioengineering major?
bare.answer: Required Courses for the Bioengineering Major (B.S. in Bioengineering). For the general B.S. in Bioengineering (separate from the Biotechnology, Bioinformatics, and BioSystems tracks), the required major courses are: Math: MATH 18, 20A, 20B, 20C, 20D, 20E. Science: BILD 1; CHEM 6A, 6B, 7L; PHYS 2A, 2B, 2BL, 2C, 2CL. Lower-Division Engineering: BENG 1; MAE 3, MAE 8, MAE 40. Upper-Division Core: BENG 100, 103B, 110, 112A, 112B, 122A, 125, 130, 140A, 140B, 152, 172, 186A, 186B, 187A-D (senior design), 188A-B; MAE 107, MAE 150. Electives: Two department-approved technical electives (plus college GE/HSS courses).
bare.note: Full required list; same as the catalog page.

bare.question: What does CSE 150A cover?
bare.answer: What CSE 150A Covers. CSE 150A (Introduction to Artificial Intelligence: Probabilistic Reasoning and Decision-Making, 4 units) covers probabilistic models used in modern AI. Specific topics include probabilistic methods for reasoning and decision-making under uncertainty, inference and learning in Bayesian networks, and prediction and planning in Markov decision processes, along with applications in intelligent systems, speech and natural language processing, information retrieval, and robotics.
bare.note: Description and topics from the catalog.

bare.question: How many units do I need to graduate from UCSD?
bare.answer: Units Needed to Graduate from UCSD. To graduate with a BA or BS from UCSD, you need a minimum of 180 quarter units, including at least 60 upper-division units (along with completing your major, college GE, university requirements such as ELWR/AHI/DEI, senior residency, and a minimum 2.0 UC GPA).

bare.question: What math courses does a mechanical engineering major need?
bare.answer: Math Courses Needed for Mechanical Engineering. Mechanical Engineering majors must complete MATH 18 (Linear Algebra) and MATH 20A, 20B, 20C, 20D, and 20E. (The major also requires MAE 107, Computational Methods, in the upper-division core.)

bare.question: I took CSE 12 and 21. What should I take next as an AI major?
bare.answer: What to Take Next as an AI Major After CSE 12 and 21. Assuming you have finished CSE 8B or 11 and CSE 20 (the prerequisites for CSE 12 and 21), your next steps toward the B.S. in AI lower-division and early upper-division requirements are: CSE 15L or CSE 29 (Systems Programming and Software Tools) if you haven't taken it yet, followed by CSE 30. Once you have CSE 12, CSE 21, and CSE 15L or CSE 29, you will meet the prerequisites for CSE 100 (Advanced Data Structures). CSE 25 (Introduction to AI), which only requires an introductory programming class such as CSE 8B or CSE 11. Math & Probability/Stats: Progress through MATH 20A-C (or 31BH) and MATH 18 (or 31AH), plus your Probability and Statistics requirement (one of MATH 181A, MATH 183, ECE 109, ECON 120A, or CSE 103). Finishing MATH 18, MATH 20C, CSE 25, and CSE 15L or 29 unlocks CSE 55, and finishing Probability/Stats, MATH 18, MATH 20A, CSE 12, and CSE 15L or 29 unlocks CSE 150A. Other Lower-Division: Complete your 4-unit General Science requirement and 4-unit lower-division CSE elective if not yet completed.
bare.note: Prerequisite chain correct (matches the course table: CSE 25, CSE 55 and CSE 150A conditions). Does not say plainly which courses are blocked now.

bare.question: What are the requirements for the bioinformatics major?
bare.answer: Requirements for the Bioinformatics Major. UCSD offers Bioinformatics through three departments, all sharing a core foundation while adding department-specific courses: Shared Core: Calculus and linear algebra (MATH 18, 20A-C), physics (PHYS 2A-C), CSE 11 (or 8A-B), CSE 12, CSE 21, CSE 100, CSE 101, genetics (BICD 100), molecular biology (BIMM 100), biochemistry, MATH 186, and the bioinformatics core series (CSE/BIMM/BENG 181, CSE/BIMM/BENG 182, BENG 183, and CSE 185). CSE (BS in Computer Science with Specialization in Bioinformatics): 128 major units total, emphasizing CS core/electives alongside BIBC 100 or CHEM 114A or BIBC 102, BICD 100, BIMM 100, BIMM 101, and the 20-unit bioinformatics series. Bioengineering (BS in Bioengineering: Bioinformatics): Adds engineering math/courses (such as MATH 20D-E, BENG 1, 100, 120, 125, 130, 168), senior design/bioengineering sequences (BENG 187A-D, 188A-B), and 8 units of engineering technical electives. Biological Sciences (BS in Biology with Specialization in Bioinformatics): Requires 48 upper-division units, including lower-division BILD 1, 3, 4, 5, CHEM 6A-B, CHEM 40A-B, CSE 11 (or 8A-B), 12, 21, MATH 18, 20A-C, PHYS 2A-C; upper-division CSE 100, 101, biochemistry (BIBC 100/102 or CHEM 114A/B), BICD 100, BIMM 100, BIMM 181, BIMM 182, BENG 183, CSE 185, MATH 186, and at least 8 units of upper-division Biology electives.
bare.note: Treats PHYS 2A-C, CSE 11 or 8A-B and CSE 100/101 as shared by every track, which is wrong for the CSE specialization (PHYS 2A only). Biology-track details not checkable against the indexed pages.

bare.answer: Prerequisites for PHYS 2A. The catalog prerequisites for PHYS 2A are MATH 10A-B, or MATH 20A, 20B, 20C, or 31BH (with MATH 20A or placement into MATH 20B or higher serving as the standard entry point). Recommended preparation is prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20B.

pasted.question: How many upper-division electives do I need for the BS in Artificial Intelligence?
pasted.answer:
The BS in Artificial Intelligence requires sixty-four upper-division units in total: twenty units of core courses and forty-four units of elective courses [1].

The forty-four units of elective courses break down into three parts: four units of ethics (CSE 194, PHIL 174, or POLI 121D), twelve units of AI electives chosen from an approved list that are not used for other core or breadth requirements, and twenty-eight units of CSE electives [1]. Within those twenty-eight units of CSE electives, you must take at least eight units tagged with Systems, at least eight units tagged with Theory/Abstraction, at least eight units tagged with Applications of Computing, and at least four additional units of CSE upper-division, graduate, or approved non-CSE courses carrying one of those three tags [1].

Please confirm these requirements with your academic advisor.
pasted.note: Correct and complete: 64 = 20 core + 44 elective, with the 4 ethics units, 12 AI and 28 CSE itemised. Better than our live answer.

pasted.question: What are the Warren College writing requirements?
pasted.answer:
After completing the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR), all first-year Warren College students must complete a two-course writing sequence, WCWP 10A-B, for a letter grade [1, 2, 8]. Invited first-year students who meet Warren College Honors Society requirements may instead fulfill this requirement by taking the two-course Warren College Scholars Seminar, WARR 11A-B, for a letter grade [3].

Following WCWP 10A-B, all students entering as first-year students must also take two Ethics and Society courses for a letter grade, PHIL 27 or POLI 27 followed by PHIL 28 or POLI 28, in which students continue developing their writing skills [2, 5]. Transfer students satisfy the Warren writing requirement by completing Academic Writing (WCWP 100) [4].

Please confirm these requirements with your academic advisor.
pasted.note: WCWP 10A-B, WARR 11A-B, PHIL/POLI 27-28. The transfer line is thinner (no extra upper-division course).

pasted.question: What is the Revelle College Humanities sequence?
pasted.answer:
The Revelle College Humanities sequence is a five-quarter interdisciplinary sequence (HUM 1 through HUM 5) in history, philosophy, and literature that focuses on major aspects of the Western humanistic tradition and meets both the humanities and writing requirements of Revelle College [1, 2].

It consists of five courses: two six-unit courses (HUM 1 and HUM 2) that provide intensive instruction in university-level writing, followed by three four-unit courses (HUM 3, HUM 4, and HUM 5) with less intensive writing instruction [1, 5]. Students must satisfy the UC Entry Level Writing requirement before registering for any course in the sequence, and HUM 1 and HUM 2 must be completed before HUM 3-4-5 [1].

Please confirm these requirements with your academic advisor.

pasted.question: What are the general education requirements at Sixth College?
pasted.answer:
Sixth College general education requires seven areas [1]. First, Culture, Art, and Technology consists of three courses (CAT 1, 2, and 3), including two six-unit quarters of intensive instruction in university-level writing [1]. Second, Information Technology Fluency requires one course [1]. Third, Modes of Inquiry requires seven courses: two in social sciences, two in humanities, two in natural sciences, and one in math/logic [1, 7].

Fourth, Exploring Data requires one course in statistical methods [1]. Fifth, Art Making requires two courses in literature, music, theatre and dance, or visual arts [1, 6]. Sixth, Experiential Learning requires one four-unit upper-division course [1]. Seventh, Upper-Division Writing requires one four-unit course (CAT 125 or CAT 125R) [1]. Transfer students may meet all or most lower-division requirements before entering through transfer agreements [4].

Please confirm these requirements with your academic advisor.

For the Bioengineering (BS) major, required lower-division courses are MATH 20A, MATH 20B, MATH 20C, MATH 18, MATH 20D, MATH 20E, CHEM 6A, CHEM 6B, CHEM 7L, BILD 1, PHYS 2A, PHYS 2B/2BL, PHYS 2C/2CL, BENG 1, MAE 3, MAE 8, and MAE 40 [1].

All major courses require a letter grade of C- or better [5]. Ten humanities and social science courses are also shown in the sample plan, though college requirements may be higher [1, 5]. Specific topics include probabilistic methods for reasoning and decision-making under uncertainty, inference and learning in Bayesian networks, and prediction and planning in Markov decision processes, along with applications to intelligent systems, speech and natural language processing, information retrieval, and robotics [3, 6].

pasted.question: How many units do I need to graduate from UCSD?
pasted.answer:
To graduate with a bachelor of arts or bachelor of science degree from UCSD, each college requires a minimum of 180 units, including at least sixty units at the upper-division level [1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8]. Within that total, students must complete a major requiring the equivalent of twelve or more upper-division courses (forty-eight or more units) [1], along with college general education and university-wide requirements [6]. For students who enrolled prior to fall 2019, there is also a maximum unit limit of 200 units, or 240 units in Revelle and Roosevelt Colleges and 230 units in all other colleges for BS engineering candidates [3].

Please confirm your graduation requirements with your academic advisor.
pasted.note: 180 units and 60 upper-division, plus the 48-unit major rule.

Right now, the required courses marked ready with all prerequisites met are CSE 15L (2 units) or CSE 29 (4 units), and CSE 25 (4 units) [1, 10]. For your math sequence, check the prerequisites yourself for MATH 20A (Math Placement Exam qualifying score, AP Precalculus score of 5, AP Calculus AB score of 3 or equivalent AB subscore, MATH 4C, or MATH 10A) and MATH 18 (qualifying score, AP Calculus AB score of 3 or equivalent AB subscore, MATH 4C, MATH 10A, or MATH 20A), and later MATH 20B and MATH 20C or MATH 31BH [1, 11].

pasted.question: What are the requirements for the bioinformatics major?
pasted.answer:
A bioinformatics major is offered by the School of Biological Sciences, the Department of Bioengineering, and the Department of Computer Science and Engineering [1]. For the CSE BS in Computer Science with a Specialization in Bioinformatics (128 total units excluding general education), students need sixty-two or sixty-four lower-division units and sixty-four upper-division units, all taken for a letter grade of C- or better unless offered P/NP only [3, 4, 5, 7].

Lower-division requirements include CSE 8B or 11, CSE 12, CSE 15L or CSE 29, CSE 21, and CSE 30 (eighteen or twenty units), two additional units from an approved CSE or technical list, MATH 20A, MATH 20B, MATH 20C or MATH 31BH, and MATH 18 or MATH 31AH (sixteen units), CHEM 6A-B (eight units), CHEM 40A or CHEM 41A (four units), BILD 1, BILD 3, and BILD 4 (ten units), and PHYS 2A (four units) [4].

Upper-division requirements include CSE 100, CSE 101, BIBC 100 or CHEM 114A or BIBC 102, BICD 100, BIMM 100, and BIMM 101 (four units each), a twenty-unit bioinformatics series (CSE 181 or BIMM 181 or BENG 181, CSE 182 or BIMM 182 or BENG 182, BENG 183, CSE 185, and MATH 186), and five upper-division electives [5]. The indexed catalog pages also provide a sample curriculum for Bioengineering: Bioinformatics (BS) [8], but do not cover the School of Biological Sciences bioinformatics course requirements [1].

Please confirm these requirements with your academic advisor.
pasted.note: Lower- and upper-division requirements and the bioinformatics series; says plainly the Biological Sciences course requirements are not covered.
